decisions.quote: In the original study by Alvarez and Oliva (2008, Exp.3), the hypothesis was supported that distractor centroids can be localized better than chance, but single distractors cannot. This finding shows that there is an ability to process visual features outside the focus of attention. In this replication we found that both multiple and single distractors can be localized better than chance. That means we could replicate the result for centroid localization, but not for single distractor localization.
decisions.location: Primary Report 36 (Alvarez & Oliva, 2008 replication report), Discussion - Summary of Replication Attempt (view lines 470-471, source char offset 840442)
decisions.reason: Prior Argon attempts timed out on the full 100-study bundle without returning decisions. In the individual primary replication report for Alvarez and Oliva (2008, Experiment 3), the authors test both components of the original finding and explicitly conclude that they replicated the centroid-localization effect (distractor centroids localized better than chance) and manipulation check, but failed to replicate the single-distractor finding (single distractors were also localized better than chance, contradicting the original null result), stating that the results were only partially replicated. The shipped 'successful' value relied solely on the aggregate dataset's single-test binary indicator rather than the primary report's mixed findings.
